findings.reason: unlike the earlier declined s6→s5 case (a dependency on an already-`done` section), §16 is unbuilt and shares the same file, so the missing edge can mis-order two in-flight dispatches into a ticker.py conflict.
findings.text: §17's prose requires it to run after §16 (both edit `reckon/crew/ticker.py`, and §16 is itself still `implementable`), but `plan-section-depends-on` carries only s3/s4/s5 and no s17→s16 edge, so a coordinator can dispatch §16 and §17 concurrently into the same file with no declared ordering

findings.reason: the section presents an option its own done-when forbids, so a node that picks the watcher route is sent down a path it must then abandon, costing a repair cycle the plan could remove by naming the row policy as the mechanism.
findings.text: §17 says it is "the node's to decide from the code" between carrying announced lifts across a restart in the watcher and holding a re-announced baseline in the row policy, but the watcher route persists `seen` (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:2223 → lift_watch.sweep) so no baseline is emitted at all, and a pane that attaches afterwards has no row to draw, failing the required "a pane attached for the first time still shows the standing lift once"; only the row-policy route — RowPolicy's per-pane `_reported` memory in reckon/crew/ticker.py:1270 — satisfies all three done-when cases together

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §17 cites `reckon/crew/lift_watch.py` and `reckon/crew/ticker.py`, both of which exist; it carries no extensionless href to mis-resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §17's done-when is measurable (restart case finds no new row; a fresh pane shows the standing lift once) and names a declared negative control ("re-announces the baseline on restart, and the restart case must then show a row").
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §17's negative control is "logged under the run directory", the durable crew runs directory, consistent with the plan's other sections.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §17 introduces no plan label, ticket number or version tag into code; `test_a_standing_lift_is_announced_once.py` and the module names read by mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §17 offers the lift-watcher route (carrying announced lifts across a restart) and the row-policy route as interchangeable, but the watcher route cannot satisfy the section's own first-attach done-when.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §17 carries one deliverable: a standing lift is drawn once, and only a grant and an end draw a row after that.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §17 states "This section runs after §16, which also writes ticker.py", yet `plan-section-depends-on` names no s17→s16 edge while the meta declares exactly this kind of shared-file ordering for s3→s5 and s5→s2.
